verses.zh: 那时，有法利赛人和文士从耶路撒冷来见耶稣，说：
verses.en: Then Pharisees[NOTE:1] and experts in the law[NOTE:2] came from Jerusalem[NOTE:3] to Jesus and said,[NOTE:4]
notes: See the note on Pharisees in 3:7.
Or “and the scribes.” See the note on the phrase “experts in the law” in 2:4.
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

The participle λέγοντες (legontes) has been translated as a finite verb so that its telic (i.e., final or conclusive) force can be more easily detected: The Pharisees and legal experts came to Jesus in order to speak with him.

verses.zh: 「你的门徒为甚么犯古人的遗传呢？因为吃饭的时候，他们不洗手。」
verses.en: “Why do your disciples disobey the tradition of the elders? For they don’t wash their[NOTE:1] hands when they eat.”[NOTE:2]
notes: ‡ Although most witnesses read the genitive plural pronoun αὐτῶν (autōn, “their”), it may have been motivated by clarification (as it is in the translation above). Several other authorities do not have the pronoun, however (א B Δ 073 ƒ1 579 700 892 1424 f g1); the lack of an unintentional oversight as the reason for omission strengthens their combined testimony in this shorter reading. NA28 has the pronoun in brackets, indicating doubts as to its authenticity.
Grk “when they eat bread.”

verses.zh: 耶稣回答说：「你们为甚么因着你们的遗传犯　神的诫命呢？
verses.en: He answered them,[NOTE:1] “And why do you disobey the commandment of God because of your tradition?
notes: Grk “But answering, he said to them.”

verses.zh: 神说：『当孝敬父母』；又说：『咒骂父母的，必治死他。』
verses.en: For God said,[NOTE:1] ‘Honor your father and mother’[NOTE:2] and ‘Whoever insults his father or mother must be put to death.’[NOTE:3]
notes: Most mss (א*,2b C L N W Γ Δ 0106 33 565 1241 1424 M) have an expanded introduction here; instead of “For God said,” they read “For God commanded, saying” (ὁ γὰρ θεὸς ἐνετείλατο λέγων, ho gar theos eneteilato legōn). But such expansions are generally motivated readings; in this case, most likely it was due to the wording of the previous verse (“the commandment of God”) that caused early scribes to add to the text. Although it is possible that other witnesses reduced the text to the simple εἶπεν (eipen, “[God] said”) because of perceived redundancy with the statement in v. 3, such is unlikely in light of the great variety and age of these authorities (א2a B D Θ 073 ƒ1, 13 579 700 892 lat co, as well as other versions and fathers).
A quotation from Exod 20:12; Deut 5:16.
A quotation from Exod 21:17; Lev 20:9.

verses.zh: 你们倒说：『无论何人对父母说：我所当奉给你的已经作了供献，
verses.en: But you say, ‘If someone tells his father or mother, “Whatever help you would have received from me is given to God,”[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “is a gift,” that is, something dedicated to God.

verses.zh: 他就可以不孝敬父母。』这就是你们藉着遗传，废了　神的诫命。
verses.en: he does not need to honor his father.’[NOTE:1] You have nullified the word of God on account of your tradition.
notes: Here Jesus refers to something that has been set aside as a gift to be given to God at some later date, but which is still in the possession of the owner. According to contemporary Jewish tradition, the person who made this claim was absolved from responsibility to support or assist his parents, a clear violation of the Mosaic law to honor one’s parents (v. 4).tn Grk “he will never honor his father.” Here Jesus is quoting the Pharisees, whose intent is to release the person who is giving his possessions to God from the family obligation of caring for his parents. The verb in this phrase is future tense, and it is negated with οὐ μή (ou mē), the strongest negation possible in Greek. A literal translation of the phrase does not capture the intended sense of the statement; it would actually make the Pharisees sound as if they agreed with Jesus. Instead, a more interpretive translation has been used to focus upon the release from family obligations that the Pharisees allowed in these circumstances.tc The logic of v. 5 would seem to demand that both father and mother are in view in v. 6. Indeed, the majority of mss (C L N W Γ Δ Θ 0106 ƒ1 1424 M) have “or his mother” (ἢ τὴν μητέρα αὐτοῦ, ē tēn mētera autou) after “honor his father” here. However, there are significant witnesses that have variations on this theme (καὶ τὴν μητέρα αὐτοῦ [kai tēn mētera autou, “and his mother”] in Φ 565 1241 bo and ἢ τὴν μητέρα [“or mother”] in 073 ƒ13 33 579 700 892), which is usually an indication of a predictable addition to the text rather than an authentic reading. Further, the shorter reading (without any mention of “mother”) is found in early and significant witnesses (א B D a e syc sa). Although it is possible that the shorter reading came about accidentally (due to the repetition of—ερα αὐτοῦ), the evidence more strongly suggests that the longer readings were intentional scribal alterations.

verses.zh: 假冒为善的人哪，以赛亚指着你们说的预言是不错的。他说：
verses.en: Hypocrites! Isaiah prophesied correctly about you when he said,

verses.zh: 这百姓用嘴唇尊敬我，心却远离我；
verses.en: “‘This people honors me with their lips, but their hearts[NOTE:1] are far from me,
notes: Grk “heart,” a collective singular.

verses.zh: 他们将人的吩咐当作道理教导人，所以拜我也是枉然。」
verses.en: and they worship me in vain, teaching as doctrines the commandments of men.’”[NOTE:1]
notes: A quotation from Isa 29:13.

verses.zh: 耶稣就叫了众人来，对他们说：「你们要听，也要明白。
verses.en: Then he called the crowd to him and said,[NOTE:1] “Listen and understand.
notes: Grk “And calling the crowd, he said to them.” The participle προσκαλεσάμενος (proskalesamenos) has been translated as attendant circumstance. The emphasis here is upon Jesus’ speaking to the crowd.

verses.zh: 入口的不能污秽人，出口的乃能污秽人。」
verses.en: What defiles a person is not what goes into the mouth; it is what[NOTE:1] comes out of the mouth that defiles a person.”
notes: Grk “but what.”

verses.zh: 当时，门徒进前来对他说：「法利赛人听见这话，不服（原文是跌倒），你知道吗？」
verses.en: Then the disciples came to him and said, “Do you know that when the Pharisees[NOTE:1] heard this saying they were offended?”
notes: See the note on Pharisees in 3:7.

verses.zh: 耶稣回答说：「凡栽种的物，若不是我天父栽种的，必要拔出来。
verses.en: And he replied,[NOTE:1] “Every plant that my heavenly Father did not plant will be uprooted.
notes: Grk “And answering, he said.”

verses.zh: 任凭他们吧！他们是瞎眼领路的；若是瞎子领瞎子，两个人都要掉在坑里。」
verses.en: Leave them! They are blind guides.[NOTE:1] If someone who is blind leads another who is blind,[NOTE:2] both will fall into a pit.”
notes: ‡ Most mss, some of which are significant, read “They are blind guides of the blind” (א2a C L N W Z Γ Δ Θ ƒ1, 13 33 579 700 1241 1424 M lat; SBL). The omission of “of the blind” is read by א*,2b B D 0237 Epiph. There is a distinct possibility of omission due to homoioarcton in א*; this manuscript has a word order variation which puts the word τυφλοί (tuphloi, “blind”) right before the word τυφλῶν (tuphlōn, “of the blind”). This does not explain the shorter reading, however, in the other witnesses, of which B and D are quite weighty. Internal considerations suggest that the shorter reading is autographic: “of the blind” was likely added by scribes to balance this phrase with Jesus’ following statement about the blind leading the blind, which clearly has two groups in view. A decision is difficult, but internal considerations here along with the strength of the witnesses argue that the shorter reading is more likely original. NA28 places τυφλῶν in brackets, indicating doubts as to its authenticity.
Grk “If blind leads blind.”

verses.zh: 彼得对耶稣说：「请将这比喻讲给我们听。」
verses.en: But Peter[NOTE:1] said to him, “Explain this parable to us.”
notes: Grk “And answering, Peter said to him.” This construction is somewhat redundant in English and has been simplified in the translation.

verses.zh: 耶稣说：「你们到如今还不明白吗？
verses.en: Jesus[NOTE:1] said, “Even after all this, are you still so foolish?
notes: Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity. Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 岂不知凡入口的，是运到肚子里，又落在茅厕里吗？
verses.en: Don’t you understand that whatever goes into the mouth enters the stomach and then passes out into the sewer?[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “into the latrine.”

verses.zh: 惟独出口的，是从心里发出来的，这才污秽人。
verses.en: But the things that come out of the mouth come from the heart, and these things defile a person.

verses.zh: 因为从心里发出来的，有恶念、凶杀、奸淫、苟合、偷盗、妄证、谤讟。
verses.en: For out of the heart come evil ideas, murder, adultery, sexual immorality, theft, false testimony, slander.

verses.zh: 这都是污秽人的；至于不洗手吃饭，那却不污秽人。」
verses.en: These are the things that defile a person; it is not eating with unwashed hands that defiles a person.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “but to eat with unwashed hands does not defile a person.”

verses.zh: 耶稣离开那里，退到泰尔、西顿的境内去。
verses.en: After going out from there, Jesus went to the region of Tyre[NOTE:1] and Sidon.[NOTE:2]
notes: For location see Map1-A2; Map2-G2; Map4-A1; JP3-F3; JP4-F3.
For location see Map1-A1; JP3-F3; JP4-F3.

verses.zh: 有一个迦南妇人，从那地方出来，喊着说：「主啊，大卫的子孙，可怜我！我女儿被鬼附得甚苦。」
verses.en: A[NOTE:1] Canaanite woman from that area came[NOTE:2] and cried out,[NOTE:3] “Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David! My daughter is horribly demon-possessed!”
notes: Grk “And behold a Canaanite.” The Greek word ἰδού (idou) has not been translated because it has no exact English equivalent here, but adds interest and emphasis (BDAG 468 s.v. 1).
Grk The participle ἐξελθοῦσα (exelthousa) is here translated as a finite verb. The emphasis is upon her crying out to Jesus.
Grk “cried out, saying.” The participle λέγουσα (legousa) is redundant here in contemporary English and has not been translated.

verses.zh: 耶稣却一言不答。门徒进前来，求他说：「这妇人在我们后头喊叫，请打发她走吧。」
verses.en: But he did not answer her a word. Then[NOTE:1] his disciples came and begged him,[NOTE:2] “Send her away because she keeps on crying out after us.”
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “Then.”
Grk “asked him, saying.” The participle λέγοντες (legontes) is redundant here in contemporary English and has not been translated.

verses.zh: 耶稣说：「我奉差遣不过是到以色列家迷失的羊那里去。」
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] he answered, “I was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”
notes: Grk “And answering, he said.” The construction in Greek is somewhat redundant and has been simplified in the translation. Here δέ (de) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied result of the disciples’ request.

verses.zh: 那妇人来拜他，说：「主啊，帮助我！」
verses.en: But she came and bowed down[NOTE:1] before him and said,[NOTE:2] “Lord, help me!”
notes: In this context the verb προσκυνέω (proskuneō), which often describes worship, probably means simply bowing down to the ground in an act of reverence or supplication (see L&N 17.21).
Grk “she bowed down to him, saying.”

verses.zh: 他回答说：「不好拿儿女的饼丢给狗吃。」
verses.en: “It is not right[NOTE:1] to take the children’s bread and throw it to the dogs,”[NOTE:2] he said.[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “And answering, he said, ‘It is not right.’” The introductory phrase “answering, he said” has been simplified and placed at the end of the English sentence for stylistic reasons. Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

The term dogs does not refer to wild dogs (scavenging animals roaming around the countryside) in this context, but to small dogs taken in as house pets. It is thus not a derogatory term per se, but is instead intended by Jesus to indicate the privileged position of the Jews (especially his disciples) as the initial recipients of Jesus’ ministry. The woman’s response of faith and her willingness to accept whatever Jesus would offer pleased him to such an extent that he granted her request.tn Or “lap dogs, house dogs,” as opposed to dogs on the street. The diminutive form originally referred to puppies or little dogs, then to house pets. In some Hellenistic uses κυνάριον (kunarion) simply means “dog.”
Grk “And answering, he said.” The participle ἀποκριθείς (apokritheis) is redundant and has not been translated.

verses.zh: 妇人说：「主啊，不错；但是狗也吃它主人桌子上掉下来的碎渣儿。」
verses.en: “Yes, Lord,” she replied,[NOTE:1] “but even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their masters’ table.”
notes: Grk “she said.”

verses.zh: 耶稣说：「妇人，你的信心是大的！照你所要的，给你成全了吧。」从那时候，她女儿就好了。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] Jesus answered her, “Woman,[NOTE:2] your faith is great! Let what you want be done for you.” And her daughter was healed from that hour.
notes: Grk “Then answering, Jesus said to her.” This expression has been simplified in the translation.
Woman was a polite form of address (see BDAG 208-9 s.v. γυνή 1), similar to “Madam” or “Ma’am” used in English in different regions.

verses.zh: 耶稣离开那地方，来到靠近加利利的海边，就上山坐下。
verses.en: When he left there, Jesus went along the Sea of Galilee. Then he went up a mountain, where he sat down.

verses.zh: 有许多人到他那里，带着瘸子、瞎子、哑巴、有残疾的，和好些别的病人，都放在他脚前；他就治好了他们。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] large crowds came to him bringing with them the lame, blind, crippled, mute, and many others. They[NOTE:2] laid them at his feet, and he healed them.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “Then.”
Here καί (kai) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 甚至众人都希奇；因为看见哑巴说话，残疾的痊愈，瘸子行走，瞎子看见，他们就归荣耀给以色列的　神。
verses.en: As a result, the crowd was amazed when they saw the mute speaking, the crippled healthy, the lame walking, and the blind seeing, and they praised the God of Israel.

verses.zh: 耶稣叫门徒来，说：「我怜悯这众人；因为他们同我在这里已经三天，也没有吃的了。我不愿意叫他们饿着回去，恐怕在路上困乏。」
verses.en: Then Jesus called his disciples and said, “I have compassion on the crowd because they have already been here with me three days and they have nothing to eat. I don’t want to send them away hungry since they may faint on the way.”

verses.zh: 门徒说：「我们在这野地，哪里有这么多的饼叫这许多人吃饱呢？」
verses.en: The disciples said to him, “Where can we get enough bread in this desolate place to satisfy so great a crowd?”

verses.zh: 耶稣说：「你们有多少饼？」他们说：「有七个，还有几条小鱼。」
verses.en: Jesus said to them, “How many loaves do you have?” They replied, “Seven—and a few small fish.”

verses.zh: 他就吩咐众人坐在地上，
verses.en: After instructing the crowd to sit down on the ground,

verses.zh: 拿着这七个饼和几条鱼，祝谢了，擘开，递给门徒；门徒又递给众人。
verses.en: he took the seven loaves and the fish, and after giving thanks, he broke them and began giving them to the disciples, who then gave them to the crowds.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “was giving them to the disciples, and the disciples to the crowd.”

verses.zh: 众人都吃，并且吃饱了，收拾剩下的零碎，装满了七个筐子。
verses.en: They[NOTE:1] all ate and were satisfied, and they picked up the broken pieces left over, seven baskets full.
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 吃的人，除了妇女孩子，共有四千。
verses.en: Not counting children and women,[NOTE:1] there were 4,000 men who ate.[NOTE:2]
notes: ‡ Although most witnesses (B C L N W Γ Δ ƒ13 33 1424 M f sys,p,h mae) read “women and children” instead of “children and women,” this is likely a harmonization to Matt 14:21. A decision is difficult here, but since “children and women” is found in early and geographically widespread witnesses (e.g., א D [Θ ƒ1] 579 lat syc sa bo), and has more compelling internal arguments on its side, it is likely the reading of the initial text. NA28, however, agrees with the majority of witnesses.
Grk “And those eating were 4,000 men, apart from children and women.”

verses.zh: 耶稣叫众人散去，就上船，来到马加丹的境界。
verses.en: After sending away the crowd, he got into the boat[NOTE:1] and went to the region of Magadan.[NOTE:2]
notes: See the note at Matt 4:21 for a description of the first-century fishing boat discovered in 1986 near Tiberias on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee.
Magadan was a place along the Sea of Galilee, the exact location of which is uncertain.
